questions.question_text:
“I put the brown paper in my pocket along with the chalks, and possibly other things.
I suppose every one must have reflected how primeval and how poetical are the
things that one carries in one’s pocket: the pocket-knife, for instance the type of all
human tools, the infant of the sword. Once I planned to write a book of poems
entirely about the things in my pocket. But I found it would be too long: and the age
of the great epics is past.”
(From G.K. Chesterton’s “A Piece of Chalk”)
Based only on the information provided in the above passage, which one of the
following statements is true?

options.A: The author of the passage carries a mirror in his pocket to reflect upon things.
options.B: The author of the passage had decided to write a poem on epics.
options.C: The pocket-knife is described as the infant of the sword.
options.D:
Epics are described as too inconvenient to write.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.question_text:
A fair six-faced dice, with the faces labelled ‘1’, ‘2’, ‘3’, ‘4’, ‘5’, and ‘6’, is rolled
thrice. What is the probability of rolling ‘6’ exactly once?

A shop has 4 distinct flavors of ice-cream. One can purchase any number of scoops
of any flavor. The order in which the scoops are purchased is inconsequential.
If one wants to purchase 3 scoops of ice-cream, in how many ways can one make
that purchase?
